markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **a uniform-to-moderate lexical-negative curriculum within the corrected HSTU**, conditional on a matched uniform-only control. Benefits remain hypotheses requiring host validation.

**Insights from the starting point and diagnosis**

1. Industrial has the largest measured training ranking-error rate, 5.05%. Harder comparisons may help, but training margins do not establish validation performance.
2. Users reject broad thematic substitutes and unsupported equipment/project matches. Lexical contrasts target these two failures indirectly; shared terminology establishes neither model difficulty nor incompatibility.
3. Users report stale interests. Missing paired-context effects prevent diagnosing inadequate recency sensitivity, and negative sampling does not directly address staleness.

**Insights from related work**

1. HSTU uses multi-negative sampled softmax [1], motivating the uniform control. R²NS supports warm-start and stochastic harder sampling [2], without validating lexical difficulty.
2. HSTU-BLaIR motivates text [3], but its pretrained representations are prohibited. Local TF–IDF supplies lexical candidates without external weights.
3. Sampling changes implicit objectives [4]; false-negative studies motivate caution [5]. Use an explicitly biased contrastive surrogate, without claiming likelihood recovery or applying unjustified log-q correction.

**Framework and directions**

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discrimination | HSTU sampled softmax | Uniform multi-negative control | Generalization |
| Confusable alternatives | R²NS curriculum | Moderate lexical negatives | Difficulty and false negatives |
| Temporal relevance | HSTU temporal bias [1] | Learned timestamp-gap bias | Missing context-effect evidence |

**Candidate assessment**

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Positive/negative considerations follow.

- **Uniform multi-negative loss: 2/7/5/8/2.** Originality: clean control / established; potential: scalable / incremental; user: finer ranking / indirect intent matching; model: targets errors / strong existing separation; difficulty: localized change / memory cost.
- **Moderate lexical curriculum: 4/6/6/6/5.** Originality: targeted combination / established components; potential: inexpensive inference / false negatives; user: targets broad substitutes and unsupported equipment matches / cannot establish compatibility; model: challenges comparisons / lexical overlap is not measured difficulty; difficulty: unchanged backbone / mining and exclusions require care.
- **Learned temporal bias: 3/7/7/4/6.** Originality: family-consistent / existing mechanism; potential: adaptive recency / sparse observations; user: targets stale interests / compatibility unresolved; model: testable context response / effects absent; difficulty: compact bias / timestamp-interface changes.

**Selected algorithm**

Build deterministic TF–IDF neighbor pools from permitted titles/descriptions, preserving identifiers, numbers and units. Operationally define moderate lexical similarity by neighbor ranks, not model hardness. Train five uniform-only epochs, then ramp lexical replacements from zero to eight by epoch 20, retaining 32 total negatives.

```text
for each causal training position:
    exclude reserved IDs, target, and user's training positives
    sample the scheduled lexical quota without replacement
    backfill uniformly to 32 unique negatives
    optimize contrastive cross-entropy through the same HSTU
```

The proposal explicitly targets broad substitutes, unsupported equipment/project matches, and Industrial’s measured ranking errors; none implies proven compatibility gains. Measure lexical overlap, model score gaps and exclusions separately. Match controls and training limits; select only by fixed macro validation HR@10. Preserve routing, seeds, diagnostics, final-nonpadding readout and one checkpoint/category. No lexical score enters inference.

idea.description: Train the corrected HSTU using a uniform-to-moderate lexical-negative curriculum, with a matched uniform-only multi-negative control. Keep one independently trained model and one selected checkpoint per category. The selected hypothesis targets broad thematic substitutions and unsupported equipment/project matches through finer discrimination, while addressing Industrial’s measured training ranking errors.
idea.motivation: Industrial has a measured 5.05% training negative-beats-positive rate and a tenth-percentile margin of 0.8873. User feedback identifies broad relevance without a supported next-choice rationale, including speculative equipment and project needs. These observations motivate testing more informative comparisons, but lexical similarity is neither history-conditioned model difficulty nor evidence of dislike. Strong training separation elsewhere, absent paired-context effects, and score-scale dependence prevent claims about generalization, collapse or recency deficits. At 10% research progress, a controlled training-only change is preferable to simultaneous architectural changes.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected HSTU architecture, optimizer and all unrelated baseline settings. Use the same configuration across all four categories initially. Run the uniform-only control and curriculum as separate experiments; deploy only the selected experiment, never their combined predictions. Each experiment trains one independent HSTU per category. Both use 32 unique negatives per valid position and the same training schedule. Their initial hyperparameters are hypotheses, not validated optima.

Use only permitted titles/descriptions. Normalize text with Unicode NFKC and lowercase; tokenize with the documented regex [^\W_]+(?:[-./+][^\W_]+)*, preserving single-character tokens, numbers and common identifier punctuation. Preserve raw text alongside tokenization settings because this tokenizer is still a heuristic for compatibility strings. Fit TfidfVectorizer with tokenizer set to this function, token_pattern=None, lowercase=False, min_df=1, max_df=1.0, no stop-word removal, sublinear_tf=True, norm='l2', dtype=float32 and no vocabulary cap. Persist the vectorizer, item-row mapping, regex, normalization settings and library versions beneath the trial directory. Empty documents receive empty lexical pools; an entirely empty vocabulary disables lexical replacements and is logged.

Use sparse cosine nearest-neighbor retrieval in bounded query blocks, initially 128 rows. Never retain the full item-by-item matrix. Retrieve the 64 highest positive-similarity nonself neighbors, resolving ties by ascending item ID. Use ranks 9–64 as the operational moderate lexical pool; this avoids the eight closest neighbors but is not validated duplicate detection. Filter known user training positives and reserved IDs at sampling time. Sample uniformly without replacement from the remaining pool, then uniformly without replacement from the eligible catalog excluding already chosen negatives. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, use all eligible items and mask missing slots in the loss. Keep the exclusion policy identical in the control. Exhaustive sparse retrieval can remain expensive; log preprocessing time and reduce block size for memory without changing selected neighbors.

Number epochs from one. Set lexical_count=min(8, floor(8*max(0, epoch-5)/15)). This gives five uniform-only warm-start epochs and reaches eight lexical negatives at epoch 20. If the filtered lexical pool is smaller than the quota, fill the remainder uniformly. Use cross-entropy over one positive and the available sampled negatives, averaged over valid causal positions. This fixed-quota, target-dependent, deduplicated design deliberately defines a biased contrastive surrogate. Do not apply naive minus-log-q correction or claim an unbiased full-catalog likelihood. A sampling-corrected alternative would require design-specific probabilities; even an unbiased partition estimate would not yield an unbiased log-loss or gradient.

Draw diagnostic samples using a separate seed-42 RNG so logging does not alter training. Record lexical similarity, current history-conditioned positive-minus-negative gaps, lexical quota achieved, known-positive exclusion rate, pool fallback rate, eligible-catalog shortages, preprocessing time, training cost and peak GPU memory. Report these by negative source and category. Negative gaps measure model difficulty separately from lexical similarity; no score-based mining or rejection is added in this first experiment. Excluding observed positives cannot remove latent false negatives, and rank truncation cannot prove that candidates are not useful variants or substitutes.

Keep inference architecture unchanged and ensure the predictor writer reproduces the trained HSTU and loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView and DiagnosisProbe(view, device). Retain run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), grounded only in measured metrics and definitions. Keep the diagnostic loader’s B x L negative tensor and sample the additional training negatives internally. Read the greatest nonzero sequence index, never count-1; mask all-padding histories explicitly. Do not infer unavailable review content, item categories, ratings, prices, stores or simulator traits.

Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all artifacts beneath the trial directory, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Retain single-GPU execution, the supplied splits, all four dataset routes and the pinned host evaluator. Use the existing authorized checkpoint-selection procedure without adding validation users or candidates. Compare the two configurations using fixed macro validation HR@10 within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; all training and failed trials count. Do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Report actual costs and unmeasured gains as unknown. Fixed seeds aid reproducibility but do not establish statistical robustness. Repeated validation selection can overfit the small validation sample, so predeclare these two configurations and avoid expanding thresholds after inspecting scores.
idea.pseudocode:
For each permitted category, independently within the current experiment:
  Build and persist deterministic local TF–IDF neighbor pools.
  Initialize the supplied corrected HSTU using the host's seed-42 procedure.
  For epoch e = 1 through the authorized maximum of 200:
    m = 0 for the uniform control;
        otherwise min(8, floor(8 * max(0, e - 5) / 15)).
    For each of exactly 200 training batches:
      Obtain the baseline causal, left-padded sequence and positive targets.
      Compute HSTU features using the unchanged backbone.
      For each valid target position:
        eligible = real catalog minus reserved IDs and user's training positives.
        Remove target explicitly as a defensive check.
        lexical_pool = precomputed neighbors at positive-similarity ranks 9–64.
        Filter lexical_pool to eligible.
        Choose min(m, pool_size) distinct lexical items uniformly.
        Backfill uniformly without replacement from eligible minus chosen items.
        Stop at min(32, eligible_size) negatives; mask missing slots.
        Compute cross-entropy over the positive and available negative logits.
      Average loss over valid positions and update the same HSTU.
      Collect source-specific diagnostics with an independent RNG when scheduled.
    Follow the existing authorized validation/checkpoint-selection procedure.
  Persist exactly one selected checkpoint and its matching configuration.
Compare complete four-category experiments only using host macro validation HR@10.
Deploy the selected experiment with one matching HSTU checkpoint per category;
never average checkpoints, fuse scores or use lexical retrieval during prediction.

originality.positive: Combines a restrained lexical curriculum with a family-consistent objective and explicit separation of lexical overlap from measured model difficulty.
originality.negative: Curriculum sampling, TF–IDF retrieval and hard-negative objectives are established; the contribution is an incremental experimental combination.

future_potential.positive: A controlled improvement could motivate better uncertainty-aware negative selection without additional inference cost.
future_potential.negative: Lexical shortcuts and latent false negatives may undermine intent matching, and no supplied evidence establishes improvement on this benchmark.

code_difficulty.positive: The HSTU backbone and inference architecture remain unchanged; modifications concentrate in preprocessing, training sampling and loss computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Deterministic sparse retrieval, user-level exclusions, variable eligible counts, memory-bounded multi-negative scoring and faithful diagnostics require more work than a loss-only change.

related_work.title: [1] Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU, including relative positional and temporal attention biases.
Uses multi-negative sampled softmax, motivating a family-consistent uniform-negative control.
limitations: Does not establish the optimal negative count or lexical curriculum for the four target datasets.
Published results do not establish gains under this pinned evaluation.

related_work.title: [2] R²NS
contributions: Supports uniform warm-start followed by progressively harder stochastic negative sampling.
Motivates avoiding immediate selection of the hardest unobserved items.
limitations: Does not directly validate lexical-neighbor sampling with HSTU.
Lexical similarity is not equivalent to history-conditioned model difficulty, and hard unknown items can be false negatives.

related_work.title: [3] HSTU-BLaIR
contributions: Provides evidence that textual representations can complement HSTU on its evaluated datasets.
limitations: Its pretrained representations are outside the permitted resources.
Retains uniform item-ID sampling and supplies no direct evidence for lexical negative mining.

related_work.title: [4] Sampled Softmax with Random Fourier Features — Rawat et al.
contributions: Studies sampled-softmax approximation and the effects of the sampling distribution.
Supports explicitly distinguishing sampling-induced objectives from full-catalog likelihood.
limitations: Does not supply a ready-made correction for this target-dependent, fixed-quota, deduplicated lexical sampler.
Does not establish recommendation gains for this experiment.

related_work.title: [5] UFNRec
contributions: Studies false negatives in sequential recommendation.
Motivates treating unobserved items as uncertain negatives.
limitations: Does not establish that title similarity identifies false negatives.
Does not validate the proposed neighbor-rank thresholds or curriculum.

related_work.title: Mixed Negative Sampling for Learning Two-Tower Neural Networks in Recommendations
contributions: Provides precedent for combining different negative sources.
limitations: Uniform and batch sampling differ from the proposed target-dependent lexical sampling.
Its results do not establish HSTU performance under this benchmark.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Highlights the importance of accounting for deterministic positive insertion when reasoning about sampled objectives.
limitations: A naive log-q adjustment does not automatically correct the proposed sampling design.
Partition-estimation arguments do not imply unbiased finite-sample log-loss or gradients.

related_work.title: scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer documentation
contributions: Documents local sparse lexical features, custom tokenization, normalization and numeric storage settings.
limitations: Default tokenization can damage compatibility identifiers.
TF–IDF overlap does not establish intent, compatibility or model difficulty.

related_work.title: scikit-learn NearestNeighbors documentation
contributions: Provides sparse cosine neighbor retrieval suitable for bounded query batches.
limitations: Sparse input uses brute-force search; batching bounds output memory but does not eliminate exhaustive comparison cost.
Deterministic ties and empty-document handling require explicit implementation.
